• Use 2FA

caption:
There Is No Democracy Without Journalism

Scott Pelley was asked about President Trump reportedly calling him a “stiff” and suggesting he was among people who “don’t care about the country.”

His response wasn’t about politics.

It was about service.

Pelley pointed to years spent covering wars alongside American troops in Iraq, Afghanistan, and Kuwait before making a broader point:

“There is no democracy without journalism. It can’t be done.”

Whether you agree with a journalist’s reporting or not, a free press is one of the institutions that allows citizens to hold power accountable.

The danger comes when we begin treating information like a menu—accepting facts from people we like and dismissing them from people we don’t.

We don’t build an informed society by hearing only voices that confirm what we already believe.

The test of a free press isn’t whether journalists tell us what we want to hear. It’s whether they are free to report facts that challenge us, our political tribe, or those in power.

A democracy requires voters.

A democracy requires elections.

A democracy requires an informed public.

And an informed public requires journalism.

Source: Scott Pelley interview with Lulu Garcia-Navarro, The New York Times.

#ScottPelley #Journalism #FirstAmendment #FreePress #Democracy
politicallyhomeless1982
 
4w
You don’t have to agree with Scott Pelley.

You don’t have to trust every journalist.

But the question shouldn’t be, “Do I like this person?”

The question should be: “Is what they’re reporting true, supported by evidence, and worth examining for myself?”

Once we decide information is only valid when it comes from people we already agree with, we stop seeking truth and start protecting our own assumptions.
